output.brief: The latency regression comes from the storage compaction tuning change (FC-7710), not from gateway 5.8. The change raised compaction threads from 2 to 6. Compaction's share of disk bytes rose from 38% to 71%. Disk use went from 41% to 97% within 5 minutes of the push, and node-side GET time rose from 61 ms to 262 ms. In every cell that received the change, p99 jumped within minutes, whatever gateway version it ran. The cell that skipped the change, aps-3, got gateway 5.8 and stayed at about 94 ms. A test rollback of euw-1 to 5.7 changed nothing. Network and traffic growth don't fit the timing. I'm fairly confident, around 90%. Don't roll back the gateway. Doing so would reopen the security hole and wouldn't fix latency. Don't pause compaction either, because backlog would grow toward disk-full. Instead, revert the tuning in one cell first and watch p99 and backlog, then extend to the other cells if it works. Consider a more moderate compaction setting afterwards. Hold off on limiting Orrin's ingest. The 10 Nov attribution job will show what drove the backlog, and the projection says backlog won't reach 15% before 13 Nov. Gateway CPU profiling is low priority.
